item.description: Brendan Fritch will take over as Northwestern High boys basketball coach this winter (December 2026) after 11 years as an assistant with the Highlanders. (Steve Barlow/For Hearst Connecticut Media) WINSTED - Brendan Fritch grew up in a basketball family. His uncle Mike has won more than 500 games in his long career as head coach of the Torrington High girls. His uncle Ric is the former longtime lieutenant of Northwestern's Fred Williams, the winningest girls basketball coach in state history, and also a basketball referee. And his own father, Tom, while not a high school coach, taught fundamentals to youngsters in the local sports leagues when Brendan was growing up in Barkhamsted. "I'd hear all the stories of what works, what doesn't, of this situation and that situation in a game," Brendan recalled. "At Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve, we'd all get together. You'd get the referee's angle, the coach's angle. As a basketball guy, I'm sitting there listening and taking it all in like a sponge." When Fritch, now 40, was asked for his high school yearbook in 2004 what he'd like to be doing in 20 years, it's no surprise he answered, "Teaching history and coaching basketball at Northwestern." And two decades later, his dream came true. item.title: John Daly has a new Masters week deal in Augusta after longtime Hooters tradition
item.description: John Daly’s Masters-week tradition in Augusta isn’t going anywhere. In fact, it’s getting bigger. Topgolf announced a multi-year partnership with the two-time major champion that will bring Daly back to its Augusta, Georgia, location during Masters week in 2027 and 2028, extending a relationship that began with his appearances there in 2026. It’s the latest chapter in Daly’s long-running connection to Augusta, one that took an unexpected turn when the city’s Hooters closed. For years, Daly was practically as much a part of Masters week as the traffic on Washington Road. He regularly set up shop at the Augusta Hooters , selling merchandise, signing autographs and taking photos with fans. According to ESPN, Daly made nearly $800,000 during Masters week in 2024. That tradition appeared to be in jeopardy when Hooters closed more than 30 company-owned restaurants, including its Augusta location. The company filed for bankruptcy in March 2025 after accumulating $376 million in debt and later moved toward a franchise-only business model. But Daly quickly found another landing spot. Augusta television station WRDW reported that Top Dawg Tavern, located almost directly across the street from the former Hooters where Daly once parked his RV, would host him during Masters week. Now Topgolf is getting into the John Daly business, too. The new partnership follows Daly’s appearances at Topgolf Augusta during the 2026 Masters and will expand beyond Georgia with appearances at Topgolf venues around the country, branded content and other experiences. “I love the vibe at Topgolf,” Daly said. “It’s a place where you can smash a golf ball, listen to music, have a drink and enjoy yourself with friends and family. That’s my kind of golf.” The partnership also includes the return of Topgolf Nights beginning Oct. 22, along with John Daly-branded merchandise and two ready-to-drink cocktails that will be offered at 55 Topgolf locations. “John Daly is a one-of-a-kind icon who completely disrupted this sport by refusing to be anyone but himself,” Topgolf CEO David McKillips said. “At Topgolf, we pride ourselves on breaking down barriers so anyone can play, which is exactly what makes this partnership so natural and exciting.” For Augusta, though, there’s more coming. Topgolf said Daly will make appearances at its Augusta location during Masters week in both 2027 and 2028, with details about a new event involving Daly expected to be announced before next year’s tournament. Daly made 12 appearances in the Masters, with his best finish coming in 1993 when he tied for third. Tim Schmitt is the managing editor of Golfweek and the golf coordinator for the USA Today Network. item.title: Book and Kovač demand Dortmund be "more ruthless" after Sabah win
item.description: Book and Kovač demand Dortmund be "more ruthless" after Sabah win After Borussia Dortmund's narrow 2-1 win over Sabah this evening , Ole Book was content but was frustrated by their lack of clinical edge. “We definitely could have helped ourselves out today by being more ruthless,” Dortmund's sporting director told DAZN at full-time. “When you travel this far — and not just us, but the fans as well — it only makes it sweeter to get the three points. "We were also critical because of our loss in Norway [to Bodø/Glimt last week]. It feels good to get a victory after three winless games. “On the other hand, we also took a significant step forward in terms of the way we played football,” he said, before Niko Kovač chimed in. “We played a really good attacking game today and created a lot of chances. If we had even capitalized on half of them, we no doubt would have won by three or four goals. “We made small mistakes here and there, which allowed our opponent back into the game. It was a tough battle, but totally deserved,” Kovač added. Dortmund's attention turns back to domestic action as they prepare for Saturday's Topspiel preparations against Eintracht Frankfurt.

item.title: Week 7 Fantasy Football Tight End Rankings: Brock Bowers Falls Behind Isaiah Likely To His Lowest 2026 Ranking
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (89) warms up before the game against the Buffalo Bills at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Christopher Trim-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It's time to set our fantasy football lineups for Week 7. We are going to turn our attention to the tight end position, which seems to completely change every week. This has been a tricky position to navigate this season. We are here to help you navigate the position and find that one tight end you want in your lineup. These are our fantasy football tight end lineups for Week 7. TE Trey McBride, Arizona Cardinals McBride is once again our top tight end in a favorable matchup against the Denver Broncos, who are slightly below average when it comes to slowing down fantasy tight ends. We are rolling with him as our top option, as we have for the majority of the season so far. TE Isaiah Likely, New York Giants Likely is the TE1 in fantasy football this season, and he comes in as our TE3 ahead of Brock Bowers. George Kittle is in our TE2 slot as the lone pass-catcher left in San Francisco, and Likely comes in right behind him. He's going to be a high-end TE1 every week unless something drastically changes with JJ McCarthy potentially taking over as the starter in New York. TE Brock Bowers, Las Vegas Raiders Bowers coming in as the TE4 is about as low as you're going to find him when he's healthy. However, we love the three tight ends ahead of him, and he has a brutal matchup this week against the Los Angeles Rams, who are allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to tight ends this season. He's still an incredible option, but we like a few other options better. TE Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers Freiermuth sneaks his way into our TE1s. Darnell Washington had a big game in Week 6, but Freiermuth will be the top option at the position in Pittsburgh. With so many injuries to the wide receivers, we expect Freiermuth to see both his volume and production increase until other players start to get healthy. item.title: Amica announces new campaign with Jayson Tatum, Boston Celtics
item.description: Amica Mutual Insurance Company has launched a new brand campaign featuring Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum according to a recent press release. This marks the company's third collaboration with Tatum, emphasizing the importance of preparation in managing the unexpected. The campaign draws parallels between Tatum's strong defensive skills on the court and Amica's commitment to providing optimal protection for its policyholders. Tatum, recognized for his defensive versatility, illustrates that effective defense is proactive rather than reactive. It involves thorough preparation and foresight. Amica, per the release, similarly anticipates customer needs, develops tailored plans for them, and assists them in preparing for unforeseen circumstances. "At Amica, we give policyholders the tools they need to protect what matters most, helping provide peace of mind," said Amica Chairman, President, and CEO Ted Shallcross. "Jayson shares our belief in the importance of preparation, making him a natural partner for this campaign." "Whether it’s defending the court or protecting what matters most, the best defense is built long before you need it," Tory Pachis, Chief Growth and Marketing Officer at Amica, said. "Thoughtful preparation is at the heart of what Jayson brings to the game and what Amica brings to our customers every day. This campaign brings that connection to life by showing that proactive preparation can make all the difference when the unexpected happens." item.title: Moreira To Race For Honda HRC Castrol Factory Team For 2027
item.description: LCR Honda rider a lock for 2026 Rookie of the Year Photos by Honda. Diogo Moreira has earned the call to the Honda HRC Castrol team for 2027, where the 22-year-old will partner Fabio Quartararo. Moreira entered the Moto3 Championship in 2022, got promoted to Moto2 in 2024, winning the championship the following season. Moreira earned five wins and 13 podiums between Moto3 and Moto2. The Brazilian rider then inked an HRC deal, setting him up with the LCR Honda team this season, in just his fifth year on the Grand Prix stage. After building up his understanding of the RC213V step by step, Moreira broke into the top ten at the Catalan GP and has since consistently fought for top Honda honors. A Sprint podium at Motegi, Honda's home race, made the case that he was ready for the factory garage. As of this writing, Moreira has outscored fellow rookie Toprak Razgatlıoğlu by a 74-18 margin, and with the 2025 World Superbike Champion's season now ending due to injury, Moreira has rookie of the year honors sewn up. "It is a fantastic feeling to arrive with the factory Honda HRC team in MotoGP, it is something that every rider dreams of when they are young," Moreira said, thanking both HRC and the LCR squad he credited as "crucial" to his adaptation to the premier class. "I am looking forward to next year and to helping Honda HRC return to where they must be." HRC Motorcycle Racing Division General Manager Yuzuru Ishikawa pointed to the Brazilian's adaptability, an important skill under the new technical regulations that arrive in 2027. "Moreira has always been able to adapt to new bikes quickly, everything from motocross to Moto3, Moto2 and now MotoGP," Ishikawa said. "We have a highly competitive rider line-up next season across Honda HRC Castrol and the LCR Team and I am sure that all of these riders will push each other not only to raise their level on track, but also to help HRC's engineers create the best bike possible in this new era of racing." With Moreira's move confirmed, the LCR Honda position will be filled by David Alonso, who signed a contract with HRC in July. Like Moreira, Alonso has had a rapid ascent, finishing third in his first full season in Moto3 in 2023 before winning the title in 2024, with 14 wins in 20 races. The Colombian moved up to Moto2 in 2025, and as of this writing, has two wins and nine podiums in nearly two full seasons. Become a Motorcycle.com insider. item.title: Arizona’s Candrea Classic to host softball giants in February
item.description: Arizona's Sereniti Trice (00) throws the ball during a Big 12 Conference softball game, Friday, March 13, 2026, at Rocky Johnson Field. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The official start of the NCAA Division I softball season is Feb. 5, 2027, but what might be the biggest campus-hosted tournament in the country will see first pitch a week later. Arizona will host Duke and former national champions UCLA and Michigan in the annual Candrea Classic beginning on Feb. 12. Opening 2027 with a bang 💥 Announcing the legendary 2027 Candrea Classic lineup! You won't want to miss it! pic.twitter.com/qUvmKt8qmo — Arizona Softball (@ArizonaSoftball) October 20, 2026 The field will include programs with a total of 21 NCAA national titles, 13 NCAA national runners-up finishes, and 62 NCAA Women’s College World Series appearances. UCLA and Arizona account for the majority of all three categories. UCLA is coming off its 34th official WCWS appearance in 2026. The Bruins rode a dominant offense to Oklahoma City where they fell to top-seeded Alabama in their opener before beating Arkansas in dominant fashion. They then lost to eventual runner-up Texas Tech in an elimination game. Duke defeated Arizona in its home regional by beating the Wildcats twice on Sunday after dropping a 10-1 game to the visitors earlier in the weekend. The Blue Devils advanced to their fourth super regional where they fell to Arkansas. Michigan advanced to the regional final in Norman, Okla. in 2026. They lost to the host Oklahoma Sooners by the score of 8-1. Arizona is coming off a 37-18 season. The Wildcats took the upper hand at the Durham regional in 2026 by defeating Marshall and Duke in the first two games. They were unable to carry over that success to Sunday when they only needed one win to advance to the Fayetteville super regional. They lost back-to-back games to Duke by scores of 8-6 and 9-4 to close out their season. The four teams were initially supposed to join a fifth team in a neutral site tournament in San Antonio, Tex. That tournament fell through, so four of the five opted to play in Tucson. The Big 12 released the 2027 conference schedule in August. The remainder of Arizona’s nonconference slate will be announced at a later date. Last year, the complete schedule was released on Dec. 17. Arizona is currently playing its fall schedule. It defeated UTEP 9-4 and 9-3 in a doubleheader on Oct. 17. The Wildcats will continue their practice games on Friday, Oct. 23 beginning at 5:30 p.m. MST. UA will host Phoenix College and Pima College in a doubleheader.

item.title: Arsenal criticism from very small minority - Arteta
item.description: Mikel Arteta led Arsenal to the Premier League title and Champions League final last season [Getty Images] Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta believes criticism of his team's playing style is only coming from a "very small minority" of observers. The Gunners have won 10 out of 11 games this season but have not been scoring freely and have struggled to break down teams that defend deep. On Sunday, they needed an 80th-minute goal from substitute Noni Madueke to edge past Nottingham Forest. It was just their 11th goal in seven Premier League games so far. The Gunners won the Premier League last season by conceding the fewest goals in the league and scoring the most from set-pieces. They have not registered a set-piece goal yet this campaign in any competition. Asked about the debate surrounding their playing style, Arteta said: "I don't have that impression because I heard that the style was incredible. We have scored so many goals, we have more possession, more shots, different players participating, no goals on set-pieces. "So the story is completely different to last year. "I think we are talking about a very small minority [criticising the team]. I think the other ones, they know. I think they have enjoyed a lot the way we have played and dominated games this year. And I think we have proven that." Arteta says there is room for improvement when they play teams with deep-lying defences. "The low block demands a different kind of game to the high block. A team that is constantly putting the ball in the last line. It's different." said the Spaniard, whose side face Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday. "I think it requires something different to the team. Still, I think on Sunday, we could have done things better. And that's in our hands. And we need to recognise that openly as well." Goalkeeper David Raya says the players are not irritated by questioning of their style, and suggests Arsenal's record so far this season speaks for itself. "People have their own opinions. The Gunners have won 10 out of 11 games this season but have not been scoring freely and have struggled to break down teams that defend deep. On Sunday, they needed an 80th-minute goal from substitute Noni Madueke to edge past Nottingham Forest. It was just their 11th goal in seven Premier League games so far. The Gunners won the Premier League last season by conceding the fewest goals in the league and scoring the most from set-pieces. They have not registered a set-piece goal yet this campaign in any competition. Asked about the debate surrounding their playing style, Arteta said: "I don't have that impression because I heard that the style was incredible. item.description: Chelsea Are Keeping A Keen Eye On This Ligue 1 Winger: Should Alonso Move In For Him? In a recent post on X , journalist Ekrem Konur claimed that Chelsea are keeping a keen eye on Strasbourg winger Gessime Yassine. It has been mentioned that the Blues are close to sealing a move for the Moroccan talent. Yassine’s Impressive Rise In French Football The 20-year-old has managed to catch the eye at times with his performances on the right side of Strasbourg’s attack in this campaign so far. Yassine has scored two goals and picked up two assists in seven matches for the French club last season in all competitions. The talented youngster is currently among the most gifted wide players in Ligue 1 . Therefore, the Blues would do well to lure him to Stamford Bridge next year. His current contract at the French club will run out in the summer of 2030, which could make it tough for Chelsea to land him on a cut-price deal this January or at the end of this campaign. FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS – JULY 08: Gessime Yassine #16 of Morocco looks on during a Morocco Training Session on July 08, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Should Chelsea Boss Xabi Alonso Move In For Yassine? Yassine is a good dribbler with the ball at his feet and can make a few dangerous runs with the ball out on the flanks. He has the vision to engineer some decent chances for his teammates to find the back of the net and can strike the ball with power from long range. The Moroccan talent has already added some goals and assists to his game. Yassine is primarily a right-winger but can also fill in as a left-sided wide player if told to do so. However, there are some question marks on whether he can cope with the physical side and high intensity of the Premier League if the Blues manage to get a deal done for him next year. We can expect Yassine to bring more quality and depth to Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso’s frontline. He is good enough to compete for a regular first-team spot at Stamford Bridge in the coming years. At 20, the future looks quite promising for Yassine as long as he continues to improve with each season. He is undoubtedly a prospect to watch out for in the long run, so Alonso would be wise to move in for him in this January transfer period or at the end of this campaign.

item.title: Worst start of Iraola era? Virgil van Dijk howler gifts Villarreal shock opener as ‘lazy’ Liverpool capitulate
item.description: Virgil van Dijk was guilty of a disastrous error as Liverpool gifted Villarreal the lead inside four minutes in their Champions League clash, stunning Anfield into silence. As the visitors lumped it forward from the halfway line, Liverpool captain Van Dijk completely misjudged his header back to Alisson, getting far too much on the ball when all he needed was a flick down. He inadvertently looped the ball up and into the path of Villarreal striker Georges Mikautadze, who controlled and finished past Alisson with aplomb to put the Spanish side in front. “Mikautadze can’t believe his luck,” Shearer said on TNT Sports commentary, who highlighted that this was Van Dijk’s third error of the match’s opening few minutes. Georges Mikautadze capitalised on Van Dijk’s error (PA) “Liverpool’s back four made an absolute mess of it after about 30 or 40 seconds, and Van Dijk has just done exactly the same there. Absolute nightmare from Van Dijk. “A clear header. You can see what he's trying to do. It wasn’t a great clearance from Alisson, and then the ball gets played over the top, and really under no pressure at all, Van Dijk just tries to guide it back to Alisson. He gets it all wrong. Too much on it.” Villarreal doubled their lead within the half-hour mark through Sergi Cardona, the Spaniards taking advantage of Liverpool’s lethargic play, with Shearer branding the side as “lazy”. “I don’t remember as bad a half an hour as this from a Liverpool team,” he said. Liverpool have won both their Champions League matches so far this season, beating Atletico Madrid 2-1 in their league-phase opener before hitting six against LASK last week. But after a rocky start, they clawed their way back to level pegging following goals from Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo before half-time. Liverpool improved vastly after the break and gained the advantage through Mac Allister’s second of the night, before Florian Wirtz scored his first of the season to give the Reds daylight.

item.title: Why Kendrick Perkins dropped cold ‘hell no’ take on Celtics’ NBA title contention
item.description: Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Why Kendrick Perkins dropped cold ‘hell no’ take on Celtics’ NBA title contention appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . ESPN analyst and 2008 Boston Celtics champion center Kendrick Perkins didn’t hold back on his take about his former team’s chances of winning a title this season. Although Perkins predicted a big season for Payton Pritchard , he doesn’t believe it will translate into a championship run in 2026-27. While some NBA analysts have high hopes for the Celtics , even without Jaylen Brown, who was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers, the team’s championship center isn’t one of them. Perkins delivered his blunt stance , per ESPN’s First Take. “The question is: are the Celtics contenders this season? And the answer is hell no,” Perkins said. “I don’t care about them winning regular season games; I don’t care about them winning the Atlantic Division. Are they legit title contenders? The answer is hell no. They don’t have the personnel. Jayson Tatum is on the clock. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “When you talk about players that are under the most pressure, Jayson Tatum is one of those guys that’s under the most pressure because of what Jaylen Brown displayed, especially in the regular season carrying this team. When you think about the city of champions — the Boston Celtics — it’s just like the Los Angeles Lakers. Championships or bust.” For ESPN’s Kendrick Perkins, the Celtics, who finished with the second-best record last season, is still a playoff team this year, but will not be one of the top seeds in the Eastern Conference. “When you look at the Celtics and their roster, I believe they’re going to make the playoffs through the Play-In tournament to be honest with you,” Perkins added. “Let’s start this NBA season off right.” “The question is are the Celtics contenders this season. The answer is hell no… They don’t have the personnel. Jayson Tatum is one of those guys that’s under the most pressure.” Thoughts on this take from Kendrick Perkins? 🤔 (via @FirstTake ) pic.twitter.com/cE09pnZUKv — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 20, 2026 Kicking off the 2026-27 NBA season, the Celtics’ starting lineup consisted of Tatum, Derrick White, Paul George, Mitchell Robinson, and Jordan Walsh in their season opener against the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday. item.title: Texas isn’t translating practice into games
item.description: AUSTIN, TX - OCTOBER 17: Florida Gators tight end Lacota Dippre #17 catches a touchdown pass while being defended by Texas Longhorns linebacker Justin Cryer #28 during the SEC football game between the Texas Longhorns and Florida Gators on October 17, 2026, at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images AUSTIN — As momentum swung in favor of the Florida Gators after a late touchdown in the first half , head coach Jon Sumrall’s team mounted a grinding, 15-play, 69-yard touchdown drive that took 8:03 off the clock and tied the game at 17-17, keeping the Texas Longhorns offense off the field for half the third quarter. The Texas defense had held Florida without a third-down conversion in the first half, but the Gators converted five straight third downs on their lengthy drive, but none was more frustrating than the final conversion, a 3rd and 3 from the 8-yard line that resulted in an eight-yard touchdown catch by tight end Lacota Dippre, his second of the game. Tramell Jones Jr. leads Florida down the field on an 8 MINUTE drive and finds Lacota Dippre for the touchdown. Tie game in Austin 🐊👀 pic.twitter.com/BkkjjZljLQ — CFB Kings (@CFBKings) October 17, 2026 The most frustrating element of the touchdown? item.title: Loan Watch: Ronald Araujo scores again for Liverpool in the Champions League
item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 20: Ronald Araujo of Liverpool jumps over the advertising boards and celebrates with the fans after scoring their 2nd goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Liverpool FC and Villarreal CF at Anfield on October 20, 2026 in Liverpool, United Kingdom. (Photo by Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo was on target again for Liverpool on Tuesday night in their Champions League tie against Villarreal. The defender was on target in Liverpool’s last Champions League outing against LASK and bagged again in Europe to make it 2-2 at Anfield. The Reds had started poorly and went 2-0 down thanks to goals from Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona. Alexis Mac Allister then pulled one back before Araujo came up with the goods again. Villarreal failed to convincingly clear a corner, allowing Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha to dink in a ball to the far post for Araujo to head home and make it 2-2 at half-time. Araujo now has two goals and an assist from three Champions League matches for Liverpool this season as he also bagged an assist against Atletico Madrid. The Uruguay international’s goal comes after he spoke about his future ahead of the match. He told a news conference how he and his family are happy on Merseyside but it’s far too early to talk about staying on past the end of the current campaign.

item.title: PSG lose Dembele, Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos in injury-plagued Barcelona clash
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain have been dealt three huge injury blows after Ousmane Dembele , Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and captain Marquinhos were all forced off in their heavyweight Champions League clash with Barcelona . Dembele sustained a hamstring issue after 19 minutes, signalling to the bench that he needed to be replaced as he held the back of his left thigh while grimacing. Follow live - PSG host Barcelona in clash of Champions League titans The Frenchman, who won the Ballon d’Or in 2025, then hit the deck with PSG manager Luis Enrique immediately turning to his bench to make a replacement. Ferran Torres came on in Ousmane Dembele’s place to face his former club (Reuters) Spain’s World Cup-winner Ferran Torres , who joined PSG from Barcelona in the summer, came on for Dembele. Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos then suffered their injuries in quick succession, with the dynamite Georgian winger suffering a knee problem before Brazilian defender Marquinhos emerged from a challenge hurt. Kvaratskhelia required two PSG team doctors to help carry him off the field and was replaced by summer signing Maghnes Akliouche. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia also suffered an injury against Barcelona (Getty) All three have been at the heart of PSG’s back-to-back Champions League triumphs, with Dembele in particular being saved for the competition by Enrique’s sparing use of the Frenchman in Ligue 1 . He has already been rested twice this campaign. However, the 29-year-old will fear this is the latest of a plethora of injury setbacks that he has endured throughout his career, something which Barcelona know all too well, with fitness issues plaguing his six years at the Camp Nou . Barcelona also endured an injury blow during the first half of the clash at the Parc des Princes , with Dani Olmo being forced off after having his ankle trodden on.

item.title: Racehorse Early Voting Dead at Age 7 After Being Diagnosed With Irreversible Colic
item.description: Sue Kawczynski/Cal Sport Media/Newscom/The Mega Agency Early Voting, the racehorse who won the 2022 Grade 1 Preakness Stakes, has died at age 7. The dark bay stallion’s owner, Dr. Padraig O’Casaigh , announced the animal’s death on Tuesday, October 20, per Bloodhorse . “After an acute onset of irreversible colic, Early Voting was humanely euthanized,” said O’Casaigh, a veterinary reproductive researcher, in a statement. John Voorhees/Cal Sport Media/Newscom/The Mega Agency “This outstanding freshman sire will not only be remembered for his tremendous success on the racetrack, but also his warm and loving personality,” O’Casaigh continued. “We would like to thank all of the staff at Taylor Made Stallions for their devoted affection and care of our wonderful mate EV.” “He loved being a Star and now he will live on through his prodigious progeny,” O’Casaigh concluded. According to Bloodhorse, O’Casaigh bought a 90 percent interest in Early Voting in July. Early Voting was the son of Gun Runner and Amour D’Ete. The racehorse became the first American classic winner for Gun Runner, per the publication. Scott G. Serio/Cal Sport Media/Newscom/The Mega Agency Early Voting was trained by Chad Brown and ridden by jockey José Ortiz in all his starts. According to the outlet, Early Voting was diagnosed with anejaculatory syndrome, a rare condition that affects a stallion’s ability to breed. O’Casaigh reportedly got involved in the horse’s life because of the research he has done addressing reproductive issues in multiple species. item.title: Kenneth Walker III Just Proved He Is The Best Chiefs Back Since 2002
item.description: William Purnell-Imagn Images Most fans expect a running back to fade after a few games. Kenneth Walker III is doing the exact opposite. He has become the first player since 2002 to record over 750 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns in his first five games. That year, it was Chiefs legend Priest Holmes who set that bar. Walker has now cleared it with room to spare. The numbers from his last game against the Chargers are wild. He gained 53 yards and scored two touchdowns on just six carries against defenses that stacked the box with eight or more players. That kind of production against heavy pressure is what changes how a team wins. The Return of a Local Favorite Walker is not just a star for Kansas City right now. He is returning to face his old team, the Seattle Seahawks. He won Super Bowl MVP honors with Seattle back in February before leaving in free agency. Now he comes back to Lumen Field as the league’s leading rusher. The Seahawks know his tendencies better than anyone because they defended him for four years in practice. But that history might not help them stop him this time. In every single matchup this season so far, Walker has run for over 70 yards. Four out of his five games have seen him find the end zone. The Chiefs have relied on him because he is playing as well as anyone in the NFL. If the Seahawks cannot contain him, they will struggle to keep the game close. Opposing backs have been held to just 96 yards per game by the defense, a top-10 mark, yet Walker is not an average back. Can He Keep This Up? People keep asking if this pace can last all year. It is a fair question given the physical toll of the position. But the writer at Sports Illustrated suggests we stop asking “Can he keep doing this?” and start asking, “What if this is just who he is?” The stats support the idea that he is evolving into a true superstar. He has a 40% forced missed tackle rate, which is the best in the NFL by a wide margin. There is also good news for the Seahawks side of the equation. Running back Zach Charbonnet might return from a torn ACL sooner than expected. A coach noted that “Zach is going to have a full week’s worth of reps, so that’s exciting. There is a possibility that you can see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that is exciting.” This adds depth to an offense that has struggled with turnovers this season. The Stakes on Sunday Night The game kicks off at 5:20 p.m. PT on Sunday at Lumen Field. The Chiefs enter undefeated, while the Seahawks look to snap a two-game losing streak. The matchup features the number one offense against a top-tier defense. If the Seahawks can stifle Walker, they have a real chance to win. If they turn the ball over again, it could be a long night. The team has already committed 12 giveaways this year, which is tied for third most in the league. Three of their first five games have seen Kansas City allow 10 points or fewer.

item.title: Atlanta Hawks strike in-market streaming deal with Prime Video
item.description: Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images As the Atlanta Hawks prepare to tip-off their season Wednesday against the Orlando Magic, the team has moved to create one of the more fan-friendly streaming arrangements in the entire league. The Hawks announced Tuesday that all local broadcasts will stream on Amazon Prime Video for fans within the team’s regional footprint at no extra cost. Anyone with an active Prime Video subscription, included with a standard Amazon Prime subscription, who lives in the Hawks’ territory spanning Georgia, Alabama, Tennessee, South Carolina, and Mississippi can stream the team’s games directly on the platform. The deal instantly makes the Hawks one of the most accessible NBA teams to stream this year. A standalone Prime Video subscription will cost Hawks fans $54 over the six-month regular season. By comparison, most other NBA teams charge more than $100 for a season-long subscription to their local broadcasts, with some charging over $200. Perhaps the only better streaming situation in the league comes from the Miami Heat, which will stream games on a direct-to-consumer app called Local 10 Plus Platinum for free. The Hawks are one of 13 NBA teams forced to arrange new local broadcast deals this offseason after Main Street Sports Group, owner of the FanDuel-branded regional sports networks, collapsed. Many of these teams have moved to local deals with over-the-air affiliates and paired them with a streaming option. The Hawks are among this group, having announced a television deal with Gray Media in July. While these deals typically benefit fans, many of whom can now access their team’s local broadcasts for free via antenna, the teams stand to lose millions in media revenue previously earned from regional sports networks. Team executives hope the increased accessibility will lead to more lucrative advertising partnerships, higher merchandising sales, and more people in the arena. Whether the limited data from teams that have already made the switch supports that is unclear. Viewership for teams that shift from cable-based regional sports networks to over-the-air networks is up across the board. So for teams willing to sacrifice some local revenue to reach more fans, moving to over-the-air is a decent tradeoff. Financial terms of the Hawks’ Prime Video deal were not reported. The deal also reportedly has an out after this season as the NBA prepares to debut its streaming hub ahead of the 2027-28 campaign. Next year, the NBA plans to launch an aggregated local streaming hub to cover most (or all) of its 29 U.S.-based teams. YouTube is reportedly the frontrunner for the package , though London-based streaming service DAZN is also expected to vie for the rights . Prime Video, which already houses NBA League Pass, the league’s out-of-market streaming service, has also been mentioned as a potential destination for the in-market hub. item.title: Why Will Wade, LSU basketball have ‘given up’ fighting for RJ Luis’ eligibility
item.description: © Gary Cosby Jr. / USA TODAY NETWORK Why Will Wade, LSU basketball have ‘given up’ fighting for RJ Luis’ eligibility appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The LSU basketball team is reuniting this season with former head coach Will Wade. Wade is back in Baton Rouge, and has put a roster together he hopes will be able to compete for an SEC title. One player Wade recruited though won’t end up playing with the team. That is guard RJ Luis. The Tigers have essentially abandoned hopes that Luis would play this season, per CBS Sports reporter Matt Norlander. “RJ Luis will NOT be cleared to play by the SEC and LSU has given up its fight for him to be eligible, sources told CBS. Luis would be in violation of the SEC’s rule that prevents players returning to college after signing a pro contract,” Norlander posted to X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Wade had essentially been lobbying the SEC to try and get Luis eligible. “Will Wade had been privately confident for months that Luis would eventually find his way to play, but the SEC would not budge. Sources tell CBS Sports that, in recent days, Wade has come to accept the reality that Luis would not be allowed to compete for LSU this season,” Norlander added. LSU basketball has high hopes this season for Will Wade Maria Lysaker-USA TODAY Sports Wade previously coached at LSU from 2017-2022 . He led the Tigers to the NCAA tournament, but the school parted ways with him over an investigation involving alleged recruiting violations. After he left LSU, Wade led both McNeese State and North Carolina State to the NCAA tournament. He is now back with the Tigers, hoping to lead LSU to a SEC championship. Even though the LSU basketball program is getting bad news about Luis, the team is getting good news about another player. “Sources also tell CBS Sports that LSU incoming center Brice Dessert, a 7-footer from France, will soon be officially cleared to play for Will Wade’s program,” Norlander added. LSU tips off their college basketball season with a game against New Orleans on November 3. item.title: He is the golfer who never won a major but led after Thursday of the 1997 Masters before an ’embarrassing’ 10
item.description: Photo by Augusta National/Getty Images The 1997 Masters is rightly remembered as the week Tiger Woods announced himself as a future icon of the game, with the boy wonder winning by 12 shots at Augusta National. Woods was making his first start in a major as a professional at The Masters. However, after taking the lead on Friday, the then-21-year-old never looked back. It is well-known that Woods played his opening nine holes of the week in 40, opening the door for another player to set the pace on Thursday. That player was John Huston, who had actually finished third on his Masters debut back in 1990. Unfortunately for Huston, his hopes of a first major victory were dashed during Friday’s second round. John Huston led The Masters in 1997 before Tiger Woods stole the show Huston went into the first major of 1997 having not won on the PGA Tour in more than three years. But there was reason for optimism that he may do well around Augusta National. Over the previous three seasons, all three of Huston’s top-20 finishes in the majors had come amidst Georgia’s iconic pines. He also missed five cuts in that run, and was disqualified from the 1995 PGA Championship for signing for the wrong score. Huston actually took the lead at The Masters thanks to an opening 67. His round had concluded with Huston holing out for eagle from 190 yards on the 18th hole. Three shots back, in fourth place, was Tiger Woods . Huston was one over par for the second round when he reached the 13th hole. However, he found Rae’s Creek with two of his shots and ended up walking away with a 10. “It was pretty embarrassing,” he said, as reported by the Los Angeles Times . “You never know what’s going to happen in this tournament.” Despite posting a second round of 77, Huston remained just outside the top-10 at the halfway stage. He was, however, now eight shots adrift of Woods. Rounds of 75 and 70 over the weekend saw Huston finish in a tie for 21st. His next top-10 in a major would come at the 2000 US Open as he finished fourth. The only problem was that Woods was 16 shots ahead of his countryman that week at Pebble Beach. Huston won four more times on the PGA Tour after the 1997 Masters, with his last victory coming in 2003. He also played in both the 1994 and 1998 Presidents Cups. However, he may not reflect too fondly on these weeks, having won one and lost seven of his eight matches in the event. Huston never played in the Ryder Cup during his career.

Woods was making his first start in a major as a professional at The Masters. However, after taking the lead on Friday, the then-21-year-old never looked back. It is well-known that Woods played his opening nine holes of the week in 40, opening the door for another player to set the pace on Thursday. That player was John Huston, who had actually finished third on his Masters debut back in 1990. Unfortunately for Huston, his hopes of a first major victory were dashed during Friday’s second round. John Huston led The Masters in 1997 before Tiger Woods stole the show Huston went into the first major of 1997 having not won on the PGA Tour in more than three years. But there was reason for optimism that he may do well around Augusta National. Over the previous three seasons, all three of Huston’s top-20 finishes in the majors had come amidst Georgia’s iconic pines. He also missed five cuts in that run, and was disqualified from the 1995 PGA Championship for signing for the wrong score. Huston actually took the lead at The Masters thanks to an opening 67. His round had concluded with Huston holing out for eagle from 190 yards on the 18th hole. Three shots back, in fourth place, was Tiger Woods . Huston was one over par for the second round when he reached the 13th hole. However, he found Rae’s Creek with two of his shots and ended up walking away with a 10. “It was pretty embarrassing,” he said, as reported by the Los Angeles Times . “You never know what’s going to happen in this tournament.” Despite posting a second round of 77, Huston remained just outside the top-10 at the halfway stage. He was, however, now eight shots adrift of Woods. Rounds of 75 and 70 over the weekend saw Huston finish in a tie for 21st. His next top-10 in a major would come at the 2000 US Open as he finished fourth. The only problem was that Woods was 16 shots ahead of his countryman that week at Pebble Beach. Huston won four more times on the PGA Tour after the 1997 Masters, with his last victory coming in 2003. He also played in both the 1994 and 1998 Presidents Cups. However, he may not reflect too fondly on these weeks, having won one and lost seven of his eight matches in the event. Huston never played in the Ryder Cup during his career.

Arteta spoke enthusiastically about the challenge ahead, praising the occasion, the opposition, and the opportunity to compete against o ne of Europe’s elite clubs. “I’m really looking forward to the game. Arsenal will face Bayern without Michael Olise, but Arteta was reluctant to describe the Frenchman’s absence as a significant advantage. Instead, he emphasized the quality of Bayern’s overall squad and the threat posed by Vincent Kompany’s team. “You want to face the best players in these kind of games, and he’s out. But when you look at their squad an d the possible starting 11 that they have, first of all, as a team, how incredibly well-coac hed they are, the mindset that they have, the conviction that they have in every action,” Arteta said. He also highlighted Bayern Munich’s ability to create dangerous moments through individual quality, adding that Arsenal would need to confront the challenge head-on. Arteta also expressed hope that Kompany would recover from his illness in time to take charge of Wednesday’s mat ch, describing himself as a huge admirer of the Bayern coach. “I’m a huge admirer of him, firs t as a person because I got to work with him for a few years. And then as a coach, in Belgium, in Burnley and wh at he’s done here—the identity and quality that his team has been showing for the past few years is on another level. Big credit to him,” Arteta said. The mutual respect between the two coaches is evident. item.title: Bulls’ Three-Center Plan Hits A Wall With Claxton Injury
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images The Chicago Bulls might not be done adding bodies to their frontcourt. Even with three centers already on the roster, new reports suggest the team is eyeing another option. This move looks odd on paper. The Bulls just signed Nic Claxton and re-signed Zach Collins. They also brought back Jalen Smith. That gives them three capable bigs for the 2026-27 season. Yet, the front office is still looking. Head coach Tiago Splitter has even talked about playing all three centers to keep fresh legs on the floor. So why chase Cisse? Claxton’s Injury Changes the Math The real reason is simple: Nic Claxton is not ready to play. The team needs help right now, not in a month. On Monday, Splitter told reporters that Claxton is “ramping up” and will be out for the next two weeks. By then he will be re-evaluated, making his target return date uncertain. That leaves the Bulls thin at center for the start of the season. They have an open roster spot after waiving four training camp invites earlier this week. Keeping that spot open gives them flexibility. But if a young, athletic player like Cisse falls into their lap, why pass? “Claxton is doing some spot shooting as we Tweet,” Bulls reporter KC Johnson said on the social media platform, X. “Splitter clarified that Claxton is progressing and will be evaluated throughout and the two-week window is just an approximation.” Why Cisse Fits the Rebuild The Bulls are in a rebuilding year. Finding young talent is the primary focus. Cisse is only 24 and stands six-foot-eleven. He appeared in 38 games for Dallas in the 2025-26 season. He brings energy and size that could help a young nucleus. The Mavericks chose to waive veteran Dwight Powell instead of the younger big man on Monday afternoon. Other teams like the Atlanta Hawks, Philadelphia 76ers, and Los Angeles Lakers were also linked to Cisse. The Hawks do not have an open roster spot. The Sixers and Lakers would need Cisse to clear waivers for a two-way deal. This fits their plan of keeping options open while hunting for upside. The front office has shown they are not afraid to move fast. They traded for Buddy Hield before camp and signed Jordan Hawkins after he was let go by New Orleans. If Cisse hits the market, the Bulls will likely be ready. The question is not if they want him. The question is if they can get him before the other teams make their move. With Claxton out, the need is real. The opportunity is right there.

item.title: SVG and Ross Chastain Return to JR Motorsports for 2027 ORPS Season
item.description: Photo by: Scott Sewell NASCAR Stars Set for Another Year With JRM JR Motorsports is bringing back two of its biggest names for the 2027 NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series season, as Shane van Gisbergen and Ross Chastain are set to compete in select races for the organization. The announcement, made Tuesday, October 20, confirms that both drivers will return to the No. 9 Chevrolet for multiple races next season. Their individual schedules have not yet been announced, but their return gives JR Motorsports another opportunity to compete for victories with two proven NASCAR Cup Series drivers. Van Gisbergen and Chastain both compete full-time for Trackhouse Racing in the Cup Series, making their additional starts in the O’Reilly Auto Parts Series an exciting opportunity for fans to see them compete in another environment. SVG Looks to Continue His Road-Course Dominance Van Gisbergen, widely known as SVG, has quickly established himself as one of NASCAR’s strongest road-course racers. The New Zealand native has brought his international racing experience to NASCAR and become a serious threat whenever the series visits a road course or street circuit. In 2026, SVG made three starts with JR Motorsports, winning at Circuit of the Americas and Sonoma Raceway. Those victories demonstrated how dangerous he can be behind the wheel of the No. 9 Chevrolet. His ability to navigate technical corners, manage tire wear and find speed on unfamiliar tracks makes him a major asset for JRM whenever he enters a race. Fans will now get another chance to watch SVG chase additional victories with the organization in 2027. Chastain Brings Aggression and Winning Potential Chastain also enjoyed success with JR Motorsports in 2026, winning the rain-shortened race at Charlotte Motor Speedway. He also earned a pole position at Dover and delivered several strong performances throughout his schedule. Known for his aggressive driving style and willingness to battle for position, Chastain gives the No. 9 Chevrolet a different strength from SVG. His experience in the Cup Series also makes him a serious contender whenever he returns to the lower division. What This Means for JR Motorsports The return of both drivers gives JR Motorsports additional firepower for 2027. The team has built a reputation for developing talent and winning races, and bringing back two successful Cup Series competitors strengthens its lineup for selected events. With the exact schedules still to come, fans will have to wait to learn which tracks each driver will tackle next season. However, one thing is already clear: SVG and Chastain will once again give JR Motorsports a chance to contend for victories in the O’Reilly Auto Parts Series.

item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). item.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
